claim: Let \(P,Q,R\in\mathbb C[z]\) be nonconstant polynomials, put \(m=\deg Q\), \(k=\deg R\), and assume \(1\le k<m\). Set \(\widetilde Q=-Q+R\). If no fundamental ray of \(Q\) is a fundamental ray of \(R\), then the entire function \(F(z)=\exp(Q(z))+\exp(\widetilde Q(z))+P(z)\) has a Baker omitted value at \(\infty\). Thus the same-degree, opposite-leading-coefficient replacement asked about in Question 6.1(1) of Das--Ghora--Nayak has an affirmative answer for every lower-order perturbation \(R\) transverse to the common fundamental rays of \(Q\) and \(\widetilde Q\).
integrity: The proof is analytic and uses only explicitly cited theorems and lemmas from the motivating preprint together with elementary polynomial growth and connectedness arguments; no numerical experiment or external certificate is used.
scientific_limitations: The resonant cases in which a fundamental ray of \(R=Q+\widetilde Q\) coincides with a fundamental ray of \(Q\) are not settled.
The full same-degree opposite-leading-coefficient question and the more general coincident-fundamental-ray formulation in Question 6.1(1) remain open outside the stated transversality hypothesis.
Broad classical value-distribution literature on exponential polynomials was not exhaustively inspectable, so an unnamed equivalent implication remains a residual originality risk.
title: A generic lower-order perturbation criterion for opposite exponential phases
